facts.text: Bring out the timpano when the dinner guests hold their breath.
facts.why: The timpano is served at the big night and is the grand dish of the feast. Neither write up I opened says the guests hold their breath, so the reaction is unconfirmed.
facts.fix: Bring out the timpano when Primo's feast reaches its grand dish.

facts.text: Timpano. The pasta drum. The room goes quiet when it's cut
facts.why: Wikipedia and the write ups confirm the timpano is the centrepiece. None of them describe the room going quiet when it is cut.
facts.fix: Timpano. The pasta drum, the grand dish of the feast.

facts.text: Roast pork, whole-pig style. Carried in on a board at the feast
facts.why: The courses include a suckling pig, so the dish is right. The sources say nothing about how it is carried in.
facts.fix: Roast suckling pig, one of the feast's courses.

facts.text: Panna cotta -- Primo's dessert, simple and perfect
facts.why: One review notes the dessert (dolci) is not described on screen, so a panna cotta cannot be confirmed.
facts.fix: Dolci -- the sweet end of the feast

facts.text: Primo's caffè corretto with grappa -- the brothers' nightcap in the kitchen after the big night
facts.why: The morning after, Secondo cooks an omelette in silence and the brothers eat it together. None of the sources mention a nightcap or grappa.

vibe.verdict: The food and the feast order are right, and the silent omelette ending is a lovely pick. The page misses the characters and the arguments.
missing: Primo on the customer: 'She's a Philistine' (kitchen)
To eat good food is to be close to God (Primo)
Louis Prima never arriving (the big night)
ideas: Swap the 'No side of spaghetti' footer for Primo's 'To eat good food is to be close to God'
Add Pascal's as the rival on a small sign, replacing the empty panel
Replace the Louis Prima line with a 'table kept for Louis Prima' card
Swap the frittata note for the three way split with Cristiano
